implementationChoicesForReview: Natural expiry stores and returns APPROVAL_NOT_VALID (contract names no dedicated expiry code).
Cancel by another actor and cancel of other terminal states: ACTION_STATE_CONFLICT; revoke by another signer, reject of APPROVED, approve/reserve of a non-approvable state: APPROVAL_NOT_VALID.
The caller's own token expiring after admission (DB clock after locks) returns ACTION_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with no mutation and no audit.
reject/revoke/reserve take the expected hash; cancel takes the request ID only.
A repeated own cancel returns the stored result, like a repeated own revoke.
reject/revoke/cancel also run the shared guard: a detected loss is committed as INVALIDATED/EXPIRED and refused, not overridden by the requested decision.
ACTION_NOT_FOUND refusals write no client audit (as S3-A get); other authorized refusals write one action.<command>_refused row.
Consumption failure code is APPROVAL_NOT_VALID for unknown/copied/spent/late/mismatched permits; a refused consumption spends the permit.

findings.summary: tests/support/pg-race.ts waitUntilBlocked(observer, null) joined pg_stat_activity from inside the observer's open transaction; PostgreSQL keeps that backend-status snapshot until transaction end, so a pool connection opened after the first poll was never seen. The larger S3-B suite changed scheduling and exposed it deterministically in m365-confirm-clock (2/2 full runs; 3/3 isolated passes; full suite without the S3-B files 341/341).
findings.diagnosis: peak cluster connections sampled at 45/100 (exhaustion hypothesis rejected); a backend sampler showed the confirm transaction waiting on the Connection row lock for ~9.9 s while the observer saw none; a standalone repro confirmed a new backend is invisible in the same transaction until pg_stat_clear_snapshot()
findings.fix: observation-only: SELECT pg_stat_clear_snapshot() before every poll; no assertion or product change

findings.summary: new m365-disable race fixture needed boundBy/boundAt (Connection_live_binding_check) and a lifecycleVersion increment when the test restores status

residualRisks: Runtime UPDATE(state) on ActionRequest and decision on ActionApproval is column-limited, not transition-limited by grant: direct runtime SQL could perform lifecycle-trigger-allowed transitions (e.g. post-reservation state moves) outside the services; identity/intent/signer/hash/epoch/binding/nonce/result columns remain unwritable.

Runtime table-level INSERT on ActionApproval/ActionAttempt: the lifecycle/lifetime/self-approval CHECKs and scoped FKs constrain rows, but timestamps written by direct runtime SQL are not DB-clock enforced.

The permit deadline uses the local monotonic clock anchored before the DB clock read (conservative by ≥1 ms); it is process-local and does not survive restart (by design; S3-C recovery covers RESERVED attempts).
Stored-signer rechecks with an equal epoch are defense in depth: the epoch proof makes them unreachable, so they are not independently testable.
Deadlock test relies on the superuser harness setting deadlock_timeout for its holder session; a non-superuser admin would need an adjusted harness.
Expiry tests use bounded deliberate waits (≈3–5 s) on the DB clock; heavy host load could slow but not falsify them.
